text: You wake up and every passenger is staring at you.
The windows are black. Your phone reads two fourteen in the morning. No signal.
The route map above the doors lists stops you never heard of.
June sits across the aisle knitting a scarf that trails the floor.
She gives you a meek sorry smile and says "Oh sweetheart not you too."
She hands you a folded sheet and whispers "Read it. Do exactly what it says."
You unfold the page. Every passenger unfolds their newspaper at the same moment.
You lift your hand. Every hand in the car lifts with you.
Rule nine. If they copy you, freeze. You hold still until the papers rustle back.
A man in a red tracksuit yanks the door handle and laughs. "Relax, it's a prank show."
The conductor appears at your seat and says "Ticket please."
You smile and say nothing, just like rule two says.
He punches your ticket with a sharp click and moves on.
June stares at the fresh hole in your ticket and goes pale.
She holds up her own ticket punched so many times it is almost lace.
She whispers, "One hole for every stop you miss."
You look down at your ticket. One hole.
